To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) EVs are an important mechanism in the neuronal differentiation process; (2) ADSCs in direct contact with neurons differentiate into neuron-like cells and; (3) ADSCs can help in PN regeneration.
neuron-derived EVs play an important role on ADSCs neuronal differentiation.

EVs derived from neurons promote ADSCs differentiation into neuron-like cells, which could be applied in the future as a new therapeutic strategy to prevent peripheral nerve injury degenerative processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic strategies for PN injury.
the potential use of neuron-derived EVs to induce neural differentiation of ADCSs.
the development of a new method to prevent the peripheral nerve injury degenerative process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuron-derived EVs are involved in neural differentiation and that neuron-like cells are able to modulate the microenvironment in acute sciatic PN injury.
ADSCs differentiated into neuron-like cell by neuron-derived extracellular vesicle cargo, and these cells could be applied in peripheral nervous system repair.
EVs are an important factor in neural differentiation of ADSDCs and that these cells may be used as a therapeutic strategy for peripheral nerve injury treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuron-derived EVs promote neural differentiation of adipose derived stem cells ( ADSCs ), which may help in the regeneration of peripheral nerve (PN).

ADSCs are a good source for cell therapy in PN injury, and that neuron-derived EVs could be used as an important source of information to understand the molecular mechanisms that lead to neural differentiation.
EVs derived from neurons could be used as a potential mechanism for ADSCs differentiation into neurons, which could be applied for PN regeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EVs are a new tool to be used in the induction of stem cells to neuronal linage, as well as, to prevent PN injury.
EVs are a potential mechanism for neural differentiation of ADSDCs, and the neuron-derived EVs carry SNAP25, miRNA-132, and miRNA-9 that could be involved in the differentiation process.
ADSCs are a good candidate for PN regeneration and that neuron-derived EVs are an important mechanism for this process to occur.
